title: Petra and the Safehouse
premise: Ada Dunmore, an interpreter for a collapsing peace delegation in Riga, has spent years laundering ugly truths into language no one can be blamed for. When her voiceprint unlocks a dormant server in Tbilisi, she discovers the 'safehouse' network that trained her as an asset decades ago is still operational — and still collecting voices. Hunted by both the handlers who made her and the delegation that disavows her, Ada joins three other voiceprint-activated survivors to burn the archive from inside its Georgian data vault. She succeeds at the cost of the only family that ever claimed her, choosing truth over loyalty and walking out of the smoke with nothing but her own unedited voice.
about_author: Ulyana Eriksen is a former conference interpreter turned novelist who writes thrillers about people paid to make violence sound polite. She lives between Copenhagen and Tbilisi and insists every interrogation scene in her books has been fact-checked by someone who'd rather not be named.

chapters.title: The Language of Denial
chapters.summary: POV Ada. During a doomed ceasefire session in Riga, Ada softens a war crime into diplomatic fog — until a delegate's coded phrase matches one she hasn't heard since childhood training. That night, a voicemail plays her own voice back to her, asking questions she never recorded. Emotional beat: the vertigo of realizing your past speaks without your permission.

chapters.title: Voiceprint
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Following the voicemail's cadence to a dead drop, Ada speaks a passphrase aloud and a server in Tbilisi wakes, streaming files stamped with her childhood codename. Among them: dossiers on four other 'voices' scattered across Europe. Emotional beat: dread curdling into purpose — the safehouse isn't a memory, it's a machine still running.

chapters.title: Persons of No Attribution
chapters.summary: POV Ada. The delegation's security chief, Halvard, quietly offers Ada extraction if she surrenders the server access; she realizes the peace process was cover for the network all along. She refuses and goes dark, contacting the first name in the dossier: a retired radio engineer in Gdańsk. Emotional beat: the loneliness of burning your last respectable bridge.

chapters.title: The Second Voice
chapters.summary: POV Marek (the engineer). Marek tests Ada with a counter-challenge before believing her, revealing the safehouse trained children as interpreters whose accents could open doors. He agrees to help but warns the others won't trust anyone carrying the old codenames. Emotional beat: cautious kinship between two people fluent in the same damage.

chapters.title: Handlers
chapters.summary: POV Ada. In Berlin, Ada and Marek find the second survivor, Ilse — now a celebrated diplomat — who denies everything and tips off the network within hours. Assassins arrive at their hotel; they escape through a service tunnel while Ilse watches from a balcony, unmoving. Emotional beat: betrayal by someone shaped by the same hand.

chapters.title: What the Archive Keeps
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Decrypted files show the safehouse records every sentence its graduates speak publicly, building leverage libraries used to steer treaties for thirty years. Ada finds her father's confession among them — he sold her to the program. Emotional beat: grief reorganized as fuel; belonging was always a transaction.

chapters.title: Assembly
chapters.summary: POV Tomas (third survivor). A disgraced forensic linguist in Marseille, Tomas joins Ada and Marek, bringing the final dossier location: the original vault beneath the Tbilisi data center. The three form a fragile found family over bad wine and shared nightmares. Emotional beat: warmth arriving exactly when it's most dangerous to accept it.

chapters.title: The Long Verification
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Crossing into Georgia under false papers, the team is ambushed at the border; Marek is captured and the network offers a trade — Ada's biometrics for his life. She learns Halvard is inbound too, playing his own endgame. Emotional beat: loyalty and truth pulling in opposite directions for the first time with real stakes.

chapters.title: Safehouse
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Inside the vault, Ada trades herself for Marek, then uses the live verification ritual — the network demands her authentic voice — to inject a purge command Tomas embedded in her speech patterns. The archive begins consuming itself as alarms cascade. Emotional beat: climax; her voice, once the chain, becomes the blade.

chapters.title: Unedited
chapters.summary: POV Ada. The team escapes as the servers burn, though Halvard slips away with a fragment of the library — a thread left deliberately loose. Weeks later, Ada testifies openly, in her own name and accent, before a tribunal that may ignore her. Marek and Tomas stand in the gallery. Emotional beat: resolution; belonging chosen, not assigned, and worth the ashes.
